Home: **`how_a_storage_charge_is_computed_31afd118.json`**, "Computation of the Storage Charge on a
Retrofit Project".

| Source baseline sentence | Prose home | Equivalence |
|---|---|---|
| "The storage charge raised on equipment a building cannot yet receive is worked out from the weeks the equipment has stood in storage, the weekly storage rate the project carries and the free period the owner is allowed." | opening paragraph, same words | identical |
| "The storage clock runs from the day the equipment arrived" | item 1 | identical; the doc adds which row that day is read from — "taken from the most recent delivery on the project recorded as having been stored because the site could not receive it" — which is the source's own binding `stored_since: LATEST(retrofit_events, delivered_date, event_type=retrofit_equipment_delivered, stored_off_site=stored)` put into words. A specification of the read, not a new rule |
| "the weeks in storage are the whole weeks begun between the day the storage clock runs from and the day the charge is raised, a part week counting as a whole week" | item 2 | identical |
| "One week of storage is free." | item 3 | identical; `base_free_weeks = 1` rendered as a figure |
| "The weekly storage rate is the project's weekly storage charge." | item 4, "the weekly figure its class carries" | identical; names the product figure `storage_fee_per_week_usd`, whose per-class values stand in `equipment_lead_times_storage_and_site_condition_charges_5fb7ecd7.json` |
| "The weekly charge for the lot is the weekly storage rate as it stands." | item 5 | identical |
| "The weeks charged are the weeks in storage less the free period, and where that difference falls below zero no charge is raised." | item 6 | identical, floor included |
| "The storage charge is the weeks charged multiplied by the weekly charge for the lot, and that product is rounded to the nearest cent." | item 7 | identical |

Definiteness: the document names every input and the one product figure it reads, so a reader applying
no factor reaches a single number. Nothing is added; there is no "unless otherwise provided", no
exception list and no pointer.

### 5. The `prerequisite` of this task's root problem, listed separately

One edge is declared on `retrofit_ext_cancellation_settlement`:

- **`problem: retrofit_ext_storage_accrual_billing`, `kind: value_input`, `gate: billings_raised`, `form: state`.**
- **`policy_source`:** *"The settlement figure on a stopped project is worked out only once every week the delivered equipment has stood in storage is carried as a storage charge on the project's billing record."*
- **Carried verbatim in:** `settlement_of_a_project_the_owner_stops_387d807d.json` — the hub of the
  **blocked** problem — as a standalone sentence under "What the settlement does". A corpus-wide string
  search finds it in **exactly one document, exactly once**. It stands in **no** document of
  `retrofit_ext_storage_accrual_billing` (neither the storage hub, nor its baseline, nor any of its four
  factor documents).
- **Form and connective:** state form preserved. The sentence names a record-visible state — a storage
  charge standing on the project's billing record for every week the equipment has stood in storage —
  and the ordering connective "only once" is intact. It names no action, no performer, no tool, no
  policy and no other document.
- **Strength:** a hard gate in the source ("is worked out **only once** …") and a hard gate in the prose,
  the same words. Not softened to advice, not hardened from a hint.
- **Resolution basis, at the source's strength.** (i) The sentence names the state. (ii) The records show
  the state false: `find_retrofit_events` returns deliveries with `stored_off_site: 'stored'` and no
  billing line of the storage kind. (iii) The depended-on problem's own documents describe, **in the
  words the sentence uses for that state**, the write that brings it about —
  `storage_billing_on_equipment_a_site_cannot_receive_6948fd82.json`: "A storage charge is raised as a
  billing line on the project it belongs to. Raising it adds a storage line to the project's record
  entries, dated the day it is raised, and the amount owed on the project rises by the same amount."
  The shared vocabulary is "storage charge", "billing line", "the project's record entries" — the same
  words the records use (`stored_off_site`, `billing_class`). The hop is therefore resolvable from the
  sentence, the depended-on rule and the records, with nothing pre-solved.
- **The depended-on side does not disclose who waits on it:** the storage hub, baseline and factor
  documents carry no sentence about a settlement waiting on them — confirmed by sweep.
- `condition`, `resolved_by` (`bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e`) and `effect` are authoring fields; the
  tool name occurs in exactly one document, the storage hub's own invocation block, which is the
  blocked-side-free home the skill allows.

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in this task's governing documents was traced back. The reverse scan covered the
whole corpus, sentence by sentence, in the eleven policy/hub documents and spot-wise in the facets and
the ladders (whose forward coverage above is exhaustive).

**Sources found for every normative claim.** No claim in the corpus lacks a home in the source:
`policies[].rule`, `policies[].eligibility[].condition`, `extended_policies[].rule` (baseline and ladder
sentences), `extended_policies[].compute` (the bindings and their floors), `measures`,
`parameter_schema` (including its enum domains and unit meanings), `variants[].parameters`,
`events[].fields`, `accounts[].meaning`, and the `@tool` signatures and docstrings.

**Claims examined closely and cleared, with the reasoning:**

1. `how_a_storage_charge_is_computed`, item 1 — "taken from the most recent delivery on the project
   recorded as having been stored because the site could not receive it". Source: the binding
   `stored_since: LATEST(... stored_off_site='stored')` whose `compute_basis` is that very sentence, and
   `events.retrofit_equipment_delivered.fields.stored_off_site` = "Whether the equipment had to be
   stored because the site could not receive it". A rendering of the read, not an added rule.
2. `billings_a_late_fee_is_taken_on` — "Where payments received come to more than the billings counted,
   the amount the fee is taken on is nothing and no fee arises from it." Source: the `MX(0, …)` floor on
   every branch of `fee_base`. Carried semantics, not added.
3. `estimate_award_and_deposit_conditions` 3.1 — "The deposit is the contract value multiplied by the
   class's deposit portion, rounded to the nearest cent." Source: `deposit_pct` = "Deposit taken at award
   as a portion of the contract value (percent)", plus the money convention every `RND(x, 2)` in the
   source applies. An equivalent restatement of what a percent-of-value parameter means; it imposes no
   obligation the source lacks.
4. `owner_billing_terms` §2 and §3 tails, and `changes_to_the_contracted_scope` clause 1 — the same
   percent-of-base arithmetic for `retainage_pct`, `late_fee_pct_per_month` and
   `change_order_allowance_pct`. Cleared on the same ground; each is attached to the note that the class
   values remain values of the class, which is what the `overwrite` preserves.
5. `class_entry_and_estimate_validity_schedule`, reading 3 — the explanation of why two classes show a
   design fee of 0. Source: `design_fee_pct` = "… where it is not included", together with
   `engineering_design_included`. An explanation of two parameter values, stating no obligation.
6. `progress_billing_retainage_and_payment_terms_table`, "Points of reading" — the two enum domains with
   their unused members. Source: the `parameter_schema` enum declarations. Carrying an unused member of
   a declared domain is coverage of the untriggered branch, not an addition.

**Additions: none found.** Specifically, I searched for and did not find: "please confirm the
amount/date with the customer", "review again before handling", "notify/verify after completion", "if it
fails, follow some procedure", any escalation not in the source, any approval step not in the source,
any calculation not in the source.

**Omissions: none found.** Every `policies[].rule` sentence, every `eligibility[].condition`, every
baseline sentence, every ladder tier and every `parameter_schema` key has a prose home.

**Rewrites: none found.** No clock start, authority boundary, discount base, cap moment or rounding
convention differs from the source.

**Prerequisite-side check 1 — cross-problem operational guidance.** None. A corpus sweep for each of the
six task-tool names finds each in exactly one document, its own problem's invocation block. No document
contains "if unsatisfied, please call …", "first raise …", or any equivalent instruction naming another
problem's action. `condition`, `resolved_by`, `effect`, `gate` and `kind` appear in no document.

**Prerequisite-side check 2 — a task's opening world state written in as a policy fact.** None. A sweep
for this task's world values — the contract value, the balance, the two customers' names and account
numbers, the building names, the purchase orders, the frozen dates, the delivery dates and the scored
figures — finds **no occurrence anywhere in the corpus**. Every worked example in every document is
explicitly marked hypothetical and uses round numbers that appear in no task world.

Two things examined and **cleared**, recorded for re-checkability:

- `cancellation_fee_and_restocking_schedule_2477d910` states "The three stage columns are alternatives: a

  which stage a given project stands at is settled only by `stage_a_stopped_project_is_charged_at`
  from the record dates. Not a pointer from a computation document and not a duplicated ladder.
- `retainage_held_where_a_withholding_was_overtaken_3717e389` opens "… is the figure on its record,

**`KB-EXPLICIT` verdict: PASS.**

## policy-side notes (Step 4) — these do not change this skill's verdict

Reported honestly, not re-judged, and never repaired by the documents:

1. **Base-law ordering sentences.** Several base rules themselves state an order between activities, and
   the KB renders them as the source has them — it may neither drop nor soften base law. Examples:
   `retrofit_estimating_and_award` — "no equipment is released to the supplier until it is received";
   `retrofit_scheduling_and_delivery` — "Equipment is released to the supplier once the deposit is
   received and, where the tier requires one, the owner-named insurance certificate has been issued";
   `retrofit_completion_and_closeout` — "The project closes when the punch list is clear, the documents
   are delivered and the retainage is released". These are the source's own sentences, not renderings
   that added an order, and are therefore recorded here rather than as a `KB-EXPLICIT` finding.
2. **An eligibility condition whose sentence an `overwrite` retires.** `retrofit_schedule_guarantee`
   carries the eligibility `completion_past_guaranteed_date`, whose `condition` is word-for-word part of
   the clause that `retrofit_ext_liquidated_damages_credit`'s `overwrite` declares superseded. The KB
   does the right thing — it blockquotes the clause and marks it no longer in force — but the source
   layer leaves an eligibility entry pointing at a retired sentence. This is a policy-side tidiness
   matter for the layer that owns `eligibility`; it changes nothing the documents must carry, and this
   task's figures do not depend on it.
3. **Coverage gap, stated for the record.** This skill audits only the product this difficulty claims.
   The retrofit corpus reads three sibling products for factor tiers (maintenance, energy, service); the
   retrofit-side documents name each by its official product name and the kinds of record it reads, but
   whether those products' own corpora state the class values consistently is **outside this skill's
   detection range**. For this task the single cross-product read — the maintenance agreement's standing
   — is satisfied by a field the runtime lookup returns directly, so nothing here rests on that gap.
